phase_0.boundary_condition: The outermost XML schema root element that seals the document and contains every directive as one register

⊢.chosen_element: empty XML document before the root element is declared
⊢.justification: no nodes or attributes exist so the state is the void before anything is named

⊣.justification: it is the closed boundary that contains the whole steering system

≻.chosen_element: directive application from schema node to LLM token generation
≻.justification: steering flows in one directed direction from the schema toward the model response

≺.chosen_element: model output fed back into the context window
≺.justification: the response descends back into the schema scope as new input

⋈.chosen_element: chained steering directives across the interaction
⋈.justification: each directive composes sequentially with the next so constraints accumulate

⊙.justification: the document describes its own structure so surface and interior are one register

∈.justification: one steering context opens into multiple arms because any of f, g, or h can suffice

∋.justification: the alternative arms rejoin by union into a single effective constraint on the response

⊤.chosen_element: accepted LLM response matching the directive
⊤.justification: the output constructively affirms the steering constraint

⊥.chosen_element: rejected LLM response violating the directive
⊥.justification: the output constructively refutes the steering constraint

⊞.chosen_element: contradictory directives held active at once
⊞.justification: two incompatible steering demands remain live without resolution

⊡.justification: once written the directive record is append-only and cannot be undone

phase_2.split_input: single steering context before directive choice
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: uninitialized XML document with no root element and no directives declared
phase_3.true_description: LLM response conforms to every active steering directive
phase_3.false_description: LLM response violates at least one active steering directive
phase_3.both_description: response conforms and violates simultaneously because contradictory directives are held live

steps.domain_action: allocate the empty XML document root before any directive is named
close the schema root element so it contains the full bulk content as one register
apply the first steering directive from a schema node toward LLM token generation
feed the model output back into the context window as new schema input
compose a second directive after the first so steering constraints chain across the interaction
declare the schema self-reference node so the document recognizes its own structure
open one steering context into alternative directive arms because any of f, g, or h can suffice
test the soft analogical association arm and affirm an accepted response
test the structural constraint arm and refute a rejected response
rejoin the alternative arms by union into a single effective constraint on the response
hold contradictory directives active at once without resolving the conflict
append the steering record to the immutable interaction log

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the IMASM assembler that translates schema directives into opcode operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: schema nodes pass directive tokens through the context window to the LLM inference engine
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the resident history bank holds every message and the steering log is append-only
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the interaction turn order determines when each directive applies
phase_5.alfs_store: the catalog at /home/mrnob0dy666/.imscrbgrmr/catalog.json stores the canonical tuple and navigator formulas

phase_6.cycle_cost: one context window token per steering directive cycle
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: uninitialized schema with no active directives
phase_6.post_cycle_state: schema holds active directives and the response log contains the model output
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0, the cycle moves directives from schema to response and back without creating or destroying information
